public_rationale: The central generalization caution is supported. The original work demonstrated specialized manipulation in a laboratory and left broader object interaction as a research goal. Marcus's hardware summary is incomplete: the report also includes vision-only cube experiments and tests unfamiliar disturbances. Support therefore does not endorse an implication that every result required an instrumented cube or that no generalization occurred.
limitations: The outcome assesses the stated inference about open-ended generalization, with the hardware description qualified.
The sensor-and-LED description should not be reproduced as a verified description of every experimental variant.
Limited demonstrated scope is not evidence that broader future applications were impossible.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's 2019 Rubik's cube robot result, achieved on a sensor-instrumented cube in controlled lab conditions, did not guarantee generalization to the open-ended real world.

evidence.explanation: The report also evaluates vision-only sensing using a cube whose center stickers were altered. This materially qualifies any implication that all results depended on embedded cube sensors; it does not establish open-ended task generalization.

OpenAI reported real transfer and robustness to unfamiliar disturbances. Those results qualify the controlled-laboratory characterization but remain narrower than dependable performance across open-ended objects and tasks.
